title: Theories of Rights and Human Rights

scenes.text: Are your rights born inside you, or granted by the state?
scenes.narration: Imagine waking up and being told that your rights exist only because the government says so. Where do our fundamental freedoms really come from?

scenes.text: School cricket ground rules versus your basic safety while playing.
scenes.narration: Here is an analogy to make this click: think of a school cricket match. The umpire makes local match rules, but your right to personal safety belongs to you naturally, whether the umpire likes it or not!

scenes.heading: Natural Rights Versus Legal Rights

columns.title: Natural Rights
items: Given by nature and human reason
Limits the power of the state
Championed by Locke and Thomas Paine

columns.title: Legal Rights
items: Cannot exist without an enforcing state
Supported by Bentham and Thomas Hobbes

scenes.narration: Early thinkers like John Locke said nature gives us rights that limit government power. But legal theorists argued that without a state to enforce laws, rights simply cannot exist.

scenes.name: Jeremy Bentham
scenes.idea: Natural rights are nonsense upon stilts; only state laws create real rights.
scenes.narration: Bentham pulled no punches! He warned that claiming natural rights against the state creates chaos, calling the very idea nonsense upon stilts.

scenes.heading: Moral Rights and Human Dignity
items: Human consciousness postulates liberty, which involves rights
Moral sense of right and wrong creates rights
Kant and Green ground rights in human dignity
scenes.narration: Immanuel Kant and T.H. Green took a higher moral road. They argued that our inner moral conscience demands freedom, making human dignity the true foundation of all rights.

scenes.heading: Karel Vasak's Three Generations
scenes.narration: Jurist Karel Vasak organized human rights into three historical waves: first came civil and political freedoms, followed by social and economic welfare, and finally collective environmental rights.

scenes.heading: Universal Rights Versus Asian Values
scenes.narration: Here is a modern debate: Singapore's Lee Kuan Yew argued Western rights clash with Asian values. But economist Amartya Sen countered that human rights and democratic freedoms carry universal value for everyone.

items: Natural rights limit states, while legal rights need enforcement
Kant and Green ground rights in inherent human dignity
Human rights evolved across three generations toward universal dignity
scenes.narration: To recap: remember Bentham's legal critique, Kant's focus on human dignity, and how rights expanded into three global generations. Master these three, and you will ace PSIR!
